item.title: Sebi's IPO nod to Cult.fit, Eswari Global Metal, Sohan Lal Commodity
item.description: Zetwerk's IPO was subscribed 31% on Day 2, while the company raised ₹2,251 crore from anchor investors, including BlackRock and Goldman Sachs.
item.dc:creator: Our Bureau
item.content:encoded: Sebi’s IPO nod to Cult.fit, Eswari Global Metal, Sohan Lal Commodity The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) approved four initial public offerings (IPOs) during the week ended Friday, October 16, according to its latest filing. The issues comprise a pre-filing by Sohan Lal Commodity Management, managed by Pantomath Capital Advisors; fresh issue-cum-OFS offerings by Eswari Global Metal Industries (DAM Capital Advisors), Cult.fit (Axis Capital); and an OFS-only issue by Indian Gas Exchange (IGX). Fusion CX IPO booked 4.45x on final day The initial public offering (IPO) of AI-powered customer experience solutions provider Fusion CX received 4.45 times subscription on the final day of bidding on Friday. The ~702 crore IPO got bids for 6,24,64,035 shares against 1,40,40,000 shares on offer, according to data available with the NSE. The category for retail investors was subscribed 5.70 times, while the quota for non-institutional investors garnered 4.50 times subscription.PTI Zetwerk IPO subscribed 31% on Day 2 The initial public offering (IPO) of Zetwerk Manufacturing was subscribed 31 per cent on the second day of bidding on Friday. The company’s ~5,012 crore IPO received bids for 5,74,99,200 shares against 18,50,66,845 shares on offer, as per data available with the NSE. The quota for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) received 37 per cent subscription, while the category for retail investors was subscribed 35 per cent.  PTI Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses Ltd on Wednesday raised Rs 2,251.23 crore from anchor investors, including BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and Nomura. The company allotted 14.91 crore equity shares to 99 funds at Rs 151 apiece, the upper end of the price band, according to a circular uploaded on the BSE website. Apart from BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and Nomura, the anchor book saw participation from global investors, including Capital Group and First Sentier Investors, along with sovereign wealth funds such as Norway's Government Pension Fund Global and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA). Marquee global institutional investors, including Capital World and Capital Research, and former HDFC Mutual Fund CIO Prashant Jain's fund 3P India also participated in the anchor allocation. Domestic mutual funds, including SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund and Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, also participated in the anchor allocation. Several insurance companies, including SBI Life Insurance and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, were among the investors.

item.title: White House lists $330.5 billion in investments in the US from India
item.description: The White House listed $330.5 billion in investments from India, including a $300 billion Reliance Industries refinery project, as part of $10.871 trillion in investments in the US.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / White House lists $330.5 billion in investments in the US from India

White House lists $330.5 billion in investments in the US from India The White House listed $330.5 billion in investments from India, including a $300 billion Reliance Industries refinery project, as part of $10.871 trillion in investments in the US.

The White House has listed investments worth $330.5 billion from India, placing the country among the leading investors in the US. | Image Credit: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 16 2026 | 9:52 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The White House on Friday listed investments worth "trillions of dollars" in the US, including over USD 330 billion from India, placing it among the country's leading investors.   The list of investments, played on loop on the White House YouTube channel, also features the USD 15 billion steel plant announced by Essar Group's Mesabi Metallics in Iowa.   In the list of countries investing in the US, there are two entries for India - one listing USD 310 billion and another USD 20.5 billion.   "Sit back, relax & enjoy the soothing sound of trillions pouring into America this Friday," the White House said in a post on X.

There was no immediate response from the White House to queries on this matter. Also Read

In March, US President Donald Trump announced that Reliance Industries was investing USD 300 billion to set up an oil refinery in Brownsville, Texas.   In May, Indian industry announced plans to invest up to USD 20.5 billion in the US on the sidelines of the SelectUSA Investment Summit.   The total investments - both from private industry in the US and foreign nations - amount to USD 10.871 trillion.   In his public rallies for the midterm elections, Trump has claimed that his administration secured more than USD 20 trillion worth of investments and commitments for the US economy.

item.title: China's trade barriers remain a hurdle to closer bilateral ties: Sitharaman
item.description: Finance Minister said that Chinese non-tariff barriers are restricting Indian exports of generic drugs, beef, and vegetables, complicating efforts to strengthen trade and improve bilateral relations ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Srinidhi Ragavendran and Ruchi Bhatia India faces growing trade imbalances with China as Beijing’s non-tariff barriers continue to restrict access for Indian products, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Friday.  “With China, I think our trade balance is against us, and it is growing exponentially,” Sitharaman said on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund meeting in Bangkok, speaking with the Atlantic Council. “China uses non-tariff barriers unhesitatingly,” and that is “the biggest hurdle in the trade between India and China.” Sitharaman cited phytosanitary rules — restrictions intended to protect against plant pests and diseases — among the barriers facing Indian exporters. She called out China for denying market access to India’s goods that have “immense” potential in the mainland, including generic drugs, beef and vegetables. India-China ties plunged into a deep freeze in 2020 after a deadly border clash, triggering years of diplomatic distrust and restrictions on Chinese investments and business ties. Relations have gradually improved since then, with New Delhi and Beijing taking steps to ease border tensions and restore high-level engagement. India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping have also renewed efforts to stabilise ties. India’s trade deficit with China has crossed $100 billion so far this year. Yet, Sitharaman said, India has not sought to retaliate with any non-tariff barriers or countervailing duties. Sitharaman’s comments come after External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said earlier this week that India isn’t “getting a level playing field in China.” Beyond India-China ties, Sitharaman also took aim at India’s trade relationship with Southeast Asian nations, describing existing trade agreements as “very skewed” against India.  While New Delhi intends to maintain its trade agreement with the Asean bloc, the terms would need to be refashioned, she said. India remains the world’s fastest-growing major economy, supported by strong consumption and investment. Sitharaman, however, flagged the country’s dependence on imported crude oil and fertilisers as a key vulnerability. The bill for those essential imports is “big and growing,” she said, adding to the flow of foreign exchange out of the country. The rupee has come under sustained pressure this year as surging oil prices swell India’s import bill, while foreign capital outflows and high US yields add to demand for dollars. The Reserve Bank of India has stepped up its defense of the currency, selling dollars and introducing measures including a special facility to meet state-owned oil companies’ foreign-exchange needs and tighter rules on currency derivatives. Those steps have helped the rupee recover from near-record lows, though the underlying pressures remain.
